Ruddick, Charisma (Persuasion) +4, DC 15 (convictions: schedule and self-preservation; the ask names no number and offers him nothing on safety; Aero is a Jedi Knight asking, not someone with authority to order him):
- 20+: he agrees to stay on the ground until Aero calls him from the settlement, on his own terms: ramp up and sealed, engines warm, and he lifts the moment anything comes at the shuttle.
- 15-19: he agrees to a fixed extension: thirty more minutes from now, ramp up once Aero is off it, then he lifts; Aero must call in when he reaches the settlement.
- 10-14: he does not move the schedule; he grants only that he will lift late enough for Aero to reach the settlement's comm and call him back on a later run if needed (no promise of when); the clock stays at about six minutes.
- under 10: he refuses flatly, keeps the clock, and says he raises the ramp in two minutes whether Aero is aboard or not.

(d6; from his convictions: no one left behind; the intention read in evt_0080; the line names his fear and offers him a way; the track they take runs toward the voice). Shuttle sensors (hidden fact, undecided until now; Ruddick's courier shuttle, a Republic Courier Corps light courier; his convictions: self-preservation makes him willing to look; no roll for willingness). What the shuttle can resolve from the ground of warm bodies lying in long grass about 300 ft away in full dark (d6):

- equal or above: breathing, slow and deep, low to the ground beyond the rails, more than one; the nearest roughly 30 ft north of the corner, close to where the track runs; at least one more to the west along the fence.

Tables fixed before rolling for amw5xodjw124w1h

Interpretation (GM ruling). Out of combat: no action economy, beats in sequence. The structured part passed the validator, but its preview order (move 15 ft, then take hold of Wick 5 ft away) would put Wick out of reach; the free text makes the intent clear (keep Wick, get off the track, go on quietly). Order used: (1) the line to Wick, aloud; the comm channel is open, so it also goes out over it; (2) the blade goes dark; Aero keeps the hilt in his right hand, thumb on the activator; (3) Aero takes hold of Wick; (4) together they step off the ruts about 15 ft to the right onto the cropped pasture; (5) they go on north toward the settlement across the pasture, about 15 ft east of the ruts and parallel to them, at a sneaking pace, for about 30 ft; the beat ends there, at the pack's response (the next decision point). The route to the settlement is the cart track north past the treeline (Wick, evt_0050; up_track option).
Hands: the right hand holds the dark hilt (thumb on the activator, as declared); the left hand still holds the drawn blaster (not holstered; nothing declared). Taking hold of Wick therefore uses the blaster hand: the back of that hand and wrist against his shoulder, the muzzle down, steering him, not a grip. A real grip needs a free hand. This is stated in the next turn context.

Wick's response (d6; convictions: no one left behind; the intention leaning toward the voice (evt_0080); this line grants that his mother may be alive and denies only that the voice is her; the blade going dark; a hand at his shoulder steering him off the track). In no result does he break from Aero this turn: the voice has not called again, he is under Aero's hand, and the move is short.
- 1: no answer; he lets himself be steered off the ruts but walks stiff, head turned to the trees, the lantern lit and lifted toward them.
- 2-3: "You don't know that." Low, shaking. He comes with the hand; the lantern stays lit, held low at his knee.
- 4-5: a long silence; he comes; when the blade goes out he looks at the lantern and slides its shutter most of the way closed: a dim slit of glow at his knee.
- 6: a whisper: "Then where is she?" He comes, and slides the lantern's shutter fully closed: full dark.
(World fact, GM placement: Wick's lantern is an ordinary hooded farm lantern with a slide shutter.)

Going unseen (the pack: darkvision 60 ft, keen hearing and smell, Perception +4, advantage by sound or smell; PACK_PROFILE). Positions at the start (evt_0103): two dogs behind, 25-40 ft; two to the left, 15-30 ft; the voice-dog ~90 ft ahead.
- Wick 1-3 (lantern lit): no Stealth roll. A lit lantern on open, cropped pasture shows the pair to anything watching; going quietly does not hide them. The pack keeps them exactly.
- Wick 4-5 (dim slit): group Stealth, Aero 1d20+3 and Wick 1d20+2 (Wick: provisional NPC value, Dex +2, no proficiency), both at disadvantage (the glow at knee height on open ground), against one pack Perception roll 1d20+4 with advantage (sound and smell), rolled first. The group succeeds if at least one of the two meets or beats it.
- Wick 6 (dark): the same group Stealth without disadvantage.
Success = the pack loses their exact place for now (it knows the area, not the spot). Failure = the pack keeps them.

Pack response (d6). Tactic 1-2 of PACK_PROFILE: lure, isolate; they do not rush a pair in the open; the pair has left the grass edge for open pasture and has not come to the lure. No dog attacks this turn in any result. The voice-dog replays only recordings it heard: Aero's new line was spoken aloud in still air with the channel open, about 90 ft from it (keen hearing), so it is available to it.
If the pack keeps them:
- 1-2: the four move up through the long grass along the west side of the track, keeping pace with the pair, staying in the grass. The voice is silent.
- 3-4: as 1-2, and the woman's voice calls again from under the trees, the same words and breaths.
- 5: as 1-2, and from under the trees Aero's own voice replays the line he just spoke, verbatim: "Wick, if that thing can wear my voice, it can wear hers. I'm not saying she's gone. I'm saying that isn't her."
- 6: the two dogs behind come out of the grass onto the pasture behind the pair, low, and fan wide, one to the south and one to the south-east, about 40 ft back, then stop: drover-work, closing the way back and pressing the pair north toward the trees; the two on the left keep pace in the grass. No voice. They do not close further this turn.
If the pack loses them:
- 1-3: the four rise in the grass and cast about, heads up, scenting, spreading along the west side of the track; none comes onto the pasture. The voice is silent.
- 4-5: as 1-3, and Aero's own voice replays the line he just spoke, verbatim, from under the trees (calling for an answer).
- 6: as 1-3, and the woman's voice calls again, the same words.
For every result where dogs move in the grass: one group Stealth for the moving dogs, 1d20+2, against Aero's passive Perception 14 (by sound): 14 or less, he hears movement in the grass to his left and behind (and, if the pack lost them, that it is spreading and searching rather than pacing); 15+, he hears nothing. The two that come out onto the pasture in result 6 are seen in the lantern light if it is lit or dim, and heard (no roll: open stubble, deliberately) if it is dark.

Wick when a voice calls (no roll): he flinches and stops, his head snapping to it; under Aero's hand he does not pull away this turn. What he does next is decided next turn from Aero's response and his convictions.

- 1-2: "Five nights."
- 3-4: "Eight. I counted."
- 5-6: "Eleven." A pause. "Every one of them."
In every band he does not say whose voice came first; that stays undecided.

Table WQ (d6, gm_hidden), Wick to s3 ("How long ago did your people reach out to the council?"):
- 1-2: "Don't know. The Warden does the comm. Nobody tells me anything."
- 3-4: "After Garrick didn't come back. She sent from the long set. In her office at the Grange."
- 5-6: as 3-4, and: "She didn't want to. The others made her."

Table R1 (s4, Aero's Insight with advantage, threshold 15):
- 9 or less: he is frightened and tired and holding himself tight; nothing reaches past that.
- 10-14: frightened; each time the voice comes it pulls at him and he holds against it; under the fear, grief.
- 15-19: as 10-14, and the settled intention felt before (evt_0026, evt_0080) is still there, still leaning toward the trees; at the word "council" something in him closes: resentment.
- 20 or more: as 15-19, and under the grief, guilt, close to the surface.

Table WO (d6, gm_hidden), Wick when the comm hisses open at Aero's collar (he knows the voice used Aero's words, evt_0275):
- 1-3: he looks at the collar and says nothing.
- 4-5: "It heard you last time," low. Nothing more.
- 6: "Don't. It heard you last time. That's how it got yours." He does not touch Aero or the set.

Table CA (d6, gm_hidden), who answers the call on the general channel:
- 1-4: nobody. Only the hiss.
- 5: a man's voice from the Grange's set, unnamed: "Get off the comm." The channel goes quiet; he does not come back.
- 6: the Warden's voice: "Get off the comm, Jedi. It listens." The channel goes quiet; she does not come back. (Her belief, evt_0004, said as hers; nothing about whether it is true.)

Table CP (d6, gm_hidden), whether any receiver on the general channel is within hearing of the five in the strip of trees:
- 1-5: none. Nothing that goes out on the channel this turn reaches the pack.
- 6: one is. Whose set it is and how it came there stay undecided. Everything that goes out on the open channel this turn is heard by the five and becomes available to the verbatim replay (evt_0003), whether and when it is used being the pack's own choice; it counts as a noise reaching them: Table PR3.
Table PR3 (d6, gm_hidden, only if CP is 6), early pack review:
- 1-4: the five hold in the strip of trees; the voice-dog keeps calling in the woman's words.
- 5-6: the voice-dog and two of the four move up out of the trees to the foot of the rise, about 900 ft from the shed, and lie up in the grass; calling resumes from there in the woman's words. None approaches the lit shed this turn (lure, don't charge).

Table WD (d6), Wick to s12:
- 1-2: He does not look at Aero. "You don't know that." About the voice. Then, to the blaster: "Rifle. For vermin. Never one of those." He stays by the door and does not help.
- 3-4: A long breath. "Okay." To the blaster: "Rifle. For vermin. Never a blaster." He will help, but stays by the door, watching it, while Aero works.
- 5-6: "Hear through it." He says it back, to himself. To the blaster: "I can shoot a rifle. Vermin, on the pasture. Never a blaster." He comes away from the door and goes with Aero to the back of the shed to help carry.

Table WC2 (d6), Wick at the first call after s12:
- 1-2: he goes still and stares toward the door; he says nothing.
- 3-5: he stays where he is. If WD was 3-6, under his breath: "Hear through it." If WD was 1-2, he says nothing.
- 6: he goes to the door and puts both hands on the plank, and stops there. He does not lift it. (If he was at the back, he walks back to the door to do it.)

Table R2 (s13, Aero's Insight with advantage, threshold 15):
- 9 or less: frightened, held tight; nothing more.
- 10-14: WD 1-2: resistance: he does not accept that the voice is not hers. WD 3-6: something in him has eased; he is listening.
- 15 or more: as 10-14, and the intention that leaned toward the trees: WD 1-2 unchanged; WD 3-4 still there, quieter, held against something; WD 5-6 it has turned: it leans toward Aero and toward getting ready, not toward the door.

Table WG (d6, gm_hidden), Wick to s14 ("Who went with her?"):
- 1-3: "Nobody. She went on her own." He does not know where she was going.
- 4-6: "Garrick. He came to the Grange door for her. They went out together." He does not know where they were going.
In every band why she went and what happened stay undecided.

Table DPC (d6, gm_hidden), the work datapad's charge:
- 1: dead. It does not wake.
- 2-6: it wakes.
Table DL (d6, gm_hidden, if it wakes), a passcode:
- 1-4: none: a shared crew slate; it opens to its work screens.
- 5-6: a passcode lock screen headed HASK MEADOW / SILO 3 WORKS; it will not open without the code.

Table DC (d6, gm_hidden, only if it opens), what is on it:
- 1-2: Work records only: daily shift logs in four hands (Haddow, Pell, Varro, G. Tolliver), the shaft under Silo Three taken down to 13.5 m, shoring set, soil and water notes, hauler loads, power and fuel use. The entries stop on one day with: "Stood down. All crew off the rise. - G.T." No reason. Nothing after.
- 3-4: As 1-2, and the day before the stand-down: "13.4 m. Obstruction, north wall. Not rock. Hand tools only. G.T. to inspect." Then the stand-down line.
- 5-6: As 3-4, and an image attached to the obstruction entry: a lamp-lit patch of clay wall at the shaft bottom and, half-exposed in it, something dark, angular and smooth, about the size of a fist, that throws the lamp back in a hard edge. No caption.
In every band: no entry after the stand-down; nothing names a shard, the System, the dogs or the night winch; the log establishes only what the crew wrote. The crew's being among the six (beyond Garrick) stays undecided.

Table HT3 (d6), the heater switched on:
- 1: nothing: the element stays cold and dark.
- 2-6: it ticks and begins to warm; a dull orange glow at its grille.

Table LK (d6 per locker, in order HADDOW, PELL, VARRO, G. TOLLIVER). Every locker: work coveralls, boots, gloves. Plus:
- 1: nothing else.
- 2: a hand lamp.
- 3: a heavy folding utility knife.
- 4: a climbing harness and a coil of line, about 30 ft.
- 5: a medpac, sealed.
- 6: a flare pistol with three flares.
Whether lamps hold a charge, and anything not named here, are not established by this table.

Roll order: WN, WQ, R1, WO, CA, CP, PR3 (if CP 6), WD, WC2, R2, WG, DPC, (Technology if DPC 1), DL (if it wakes), DC (if it opens), HT3, LK x4.

Table HF (d6, gm_hidden), rolled first, GM decision fixed now, the fault (the sled stood unused since the crew stopped, about two weeks):
- 1-2 DRAINED: the sled's power cell is drained flat, deeper than this wall charger will start on; the charger's cutoff refuses it and nothing flows. The gauge is honest. The sled will not run on this cell. No bench charger or spare sled cell is in the shed.
- 3-4 CLAY: the sled's charging socket is packed with dried grey clay; the plug's pins never meet the contacts and nothing has flowed since the lead went in. The cell holds what it held when the crew stopped: low. The sled can run on it, for a time not established.
- 5-6 FUSE: the gauge's own fuse behind the stand panel has blown; the gauge can show nothing. The lead passes current and the cell has been charging since it went in; with what it held, it holds some charge. The sled can run, for a time not established.
Technology bands (no hidden DC):
- 9 or less: the lead is seated, the wall socket live, the gauge dark; in the time he cannot tell whether the fault is the lead, the gauge or the cell.
- 10-14: he finds the HF fault by what he can see: DRAINED: lead and socket clean, the plug's small charge light flickers on and drops out every few seconds: the charger is trying and refusing; the cell is too drained for it. CLAY: with the plug drawn, the sled's socket is packed solid with dried grey clay; the pins never met. FUSE: behind the stand's panel the gauge's fuse is black; the lead is passing current; the gauge cannot show what the cell holds.
- 15 or more: as 10-14, and: DRAINED: a cell this drained needs a bench charger or a fresh cell; there is neither in the shed. CLAY: the clay could be picked out with a blade or a pick in a few minutes (not done: no step is added). FUSE: a standard cartridge fuse; no spare in sight; without a gauge the cell's level cannot be read.

- DRAINED: nothing; the stand stays dark; no sound. The sled does not run.
- CLAY: the stand lights; the gauge shows one bar of ten, blinking; the repulsors whine up and the loaded sled lifts about a hand's width off its stand, nose-heavy, and idles there.
- FUSE: the stand lights except the gauge, which stays dark; the repulsors whine up and the loaded sled lifts about a hand's width off its stand and idles there.
The player declared no step to turn it off: a running sled keeps idling (no step is added). Noise: a running sled's idle whine inside the shut shed: Table PN (only if it runs). How long it runs is not established.

Table WH2 (d6), Wick if the sled runs: 1-3 he turns to look at the sled, then back to the door; no words. 4-5 "It goes." 6 "It's loud. Will they hear that?" He looks at the door.

Table WLR (d6), Wick to s10-s11:
- 1-2: "In her office. She won't let you near it." Nothing more.
- 3-4: "In her office, at the Grange. She sent on it when Garrick didn't come back. She'll want to know what for."

In every band he adds nothing about the six, the voice, the shard, Garrick's role or the seed vault.
